messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

"The model that only uses answers (MLP-A) performs significantly worse than the model that observes all three sources of information." -- cites: E1 (Section D.2): quote "the performance is close to random (on the column of IoU +QoU-decoys), and far from observing all three sources of information (MLP-IQA)."
3. "The performance of the model that only uses answers is close to random, indicating poor performance." -- cites: E1 (Section D.2): quote "the performance is close to random (on the column of IoU +QoU-decoys), and far from observing all three sources of information (MLP-IQA)."

As shown in Table 8 , we clearly see that with only answers being visible to the model (MLP-A), the performance is close to random (on the column of IoU +QoU-decoys), and far from observing all three sources of information (MLP-IQA). Meanwhile, models that can observe either images and answers (MLP-IA) or questions and answers (MLP-QA) fail to predict as good as the model that observe all three sources of information. verdicts.reason: The evidence states that models observing all three sources of information (images, questions, and answers) perform better than models observing only images and answers (MLP-IA) or questions and answers (MLP-QA).
The evidence indicates that the model using only answers (MLP-A) performs close to random and far from the model observing all three sources of information (MLP-IQA).
The evidence confirms that the model using only answers (MLP-A) performs close to random, indicating poor performance.
